newsitem.title: USA: Transco plans work on Texas gas line in May.
newsitem.headline: Transco plans work on Texas gas line in May.

text.p: Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Corp said it plans on May 10 to begin major construction work on a segment of its natural gas pipeline in Texas.

In a notice to shippers, the company said smart pigging and line replacement of mainline "A" from Station 30 (M.P. 258.43) near El Campo, Texas, to valve 35A15 located 20 miles downstream of Station 35 (M.P. 346.72) near Houston, Texas, is scheduled to begin on May 10 and end on June 5.

The notice said all capacity on the line would be cut from May 14-19, with 200 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of capacity available from May 20-22. At all other times between May 10 and June 5, the line should be flowing at its listed capacity of approximately 600 mmcfd.
The notice said there were available interconnects that may be utilized to redirect gas off of Transco's system upstream of Station 30 during the above outage periods.
Transco, a unit of The Williams Cos, owns and operates a 10,000 mile pipeline system that runs from stations in south Texas and Louisiana to New York.
